Due to its small size and low weight, the wielder can carry it around comfortably with no interference during daily tasks.

A small insectoid genetically modified to produce small batches of luciferium extract every few days. Even though they are useful as a source of the dangerous drug, the internal processes generating the luciferium make luciferbugs prone to violent detonation if damaged.

If they detonate, it releases all the luciferium accumulating on their abdomens, subjecting any nearby creatures to dangerous exposure levels of luciferium.

A device that continuously conducts simulations and experiments on connected users using scarlet mechanites. The screen displays collected data in the form of reports and insights for medical staff. It connects to hospital beds.

A machine that can pump out a massive dose of scarlet mechanites. People without any mechanite tolerance will fall into a five-day-long coma due to the sudden shock and will develop a Luciferium addiction need, whereas those with tolerance will only suffer for one day without further consequences. A successful operation evokes full body resurrection. The machine deconstructs itself after three uses and requires twelve Luciferium per operation.
A very finely blended powder made from luciferium. When applied to a gourmet meal, it provides a very diluted version of the drug without risk of addictions.

A complex machine designed for precise manipulation of very small objects. It is capable of putting together scarlet mechanites into consumable Luciferium. During every operation, some material is lost due to particles instability. It can be avoided, to some degree, with higher hydraulic accuracy, which can be achieved with the help of other supporting machines.
      
It should be plugged to a net with an active scarlet refinery.

A rare and powerful substance that enhances memory and learning capacity, with a slight initial boost to psyfocus, making it highly sought after by those seeking mental clarity and rapid skill development.
A mixture of luhix. Needs further brewing in order to be used.
A bundle of seeds for lullabloom. Opening this seed bundle will allow the crop to be planted by your faction.
A vintage steel lunch box.
A vintage steel lunch box.

A high-tech device that can be installed onto a kidney or any compatible artificial kidney replacement. This particular model utilizes specialized mechanites and advanced filtration systems specifically engineered to detect and combat lung rot, granting complete immunity to it. It is largely ineffective against other diseases and infections.
A bundle of seeds for lupine. Opening this seed bundle will allow the crop to be planted by your faction.

Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Despite it possessing a trunk, macrauchenia's nostrils are actually located on the top of its head.
It's extraordinarily agile and thanks to its ability of rapidly changing directions while running at high speed, it can escape most predators fairly easily.
Raw butchered flesh. Can be cooked into meals, or eaten raw.

A medium-sized bioengineered flying insectoid the size of a pig. The macrofly is the lowest caste of the Chelis hive, responsible for most of the resource gathering and work. It’s capable of lunging towards enemies at incredible speed, and it uses the digging claws to rip them in close quarters. It's dangerous in combat, but slow on open ground.

While the user is safe from being directly affected by the module, it will damage any nearby machinery and implants that are vulnerable to EMP attacks, regardless of who they belong to.

A high-tech animal implant that can be installed onto the spine or any compatible artificial spine replacement. This particular module comes with a set of advanced artificial micro-organs that are capable of emitting short-ranged directional electromagnetic pulses. The EMP disturbances are emitted upon performing a melee attack, allowing its host to stun mechanoids and halt the functionality of electronic equipment with each bite, scratch or strike.

A sharp piece of rock mounted on a sturdy piece of wood. Often used as a tool, it has been recorded that tribal axes also served as a great weapon due to their small size and ability to inflict deep wounds.

An improvised, gas-operated light machine gun. Unwieldy and inaccurate, it is also very prone to jamming. Its long bursts of fire are effective against groups of enemies, but their shot counts are completely random.
An improvised, rough, ancient-design pattern blowback-operated self-loading pistol. It lacks stopping power and range and is prone to jamming.

A general-purpose gas-operated improvised assault rifle, utilising various salvaged components mounted on a militia rifle receiver. It has good range, decent power, and good accuracy, but is prone to jamming.
An improvised design powerful shotgun that emits a large barrage of pellets. Deadly, but short range. Due to numerous faults in design, the amount of pellets fired varies shot by shot.
A small, home-made micro-submachine gun. It's short range and very prone to jamming due to the rough design and faulty elements. Its rate of fire tends to make up for its weakness.
Sturdy pieces of wood lashed together with leather or fabric for storing large quantities of weaponry. Does not prevent deterioration. Prevents weaponry from affecting the beauty of its surroundings.

A highly concentrated mixture of antibodies enhanced with spacer technology that rapidly spreads through the user's bloodstream. It can be ingested, granting instant immunity to malaria. Powerful glitterworld medicine makes it highly effective and capable of killing even parasites.
A barrel full of malaria gas. Ignites upon getting shot, which results in a massive gas explosion infecting everyone around it.
A military-grade malaria gas grenade launcher intended for anti-infantry use.
A shell filled with malaria gas. Can be fired from mortars. Explodes when damaged infecting everyone nearby.

A high-tech device that can be installed onto a kidney or any compatible artificial kidney replacement. This particular model utilizes specialized mechanites and advanced filtration systems specifically engineered to detect and combat malaria along with neutralizing the parasite causing the condition, granting complete immunity to it. It is largely ineffective against other diseases and infections.
A malaria parasite pathogen that's a crucial ingredient in producing biological weapons. It must be kept indoors at freezing temperatures to stay fresh and usable.

A sample of malaria parasite. Can be used in production of special reproduction pills that will produce malaria pathogens after consumption.

Can be obtained by using disease sampler on a living creature infected with malaria or crafted from malaria pathogens.

A drug containing malaria parasite embryos with enhanced reproduction capabilities. Whoever consumes it will turn into a living pathogen breeding machine. The host's body will continuously spew out malaria pathogens and receive internal damage in the process. If left untended, he will die and produce fewer pathogens. 

Note that large, tamed creatures in herds are best suited for being hosts.

A syringe containing a carefully prepared mixture of antigens. It prevents getting sick from malaria for 8 days and provides full protection from malaria pathogen gas.

Note that it does not cure existing infections.
Badly rusted mall bench.
A bench at the mall.
Wooden benches at the mall.

A simple yet versatile tool featuring a solid head, typically made of wood, rubber, or metal, attached to a sturdy handle. Designed for delivering controlled force without damaging delicate surfaces, it serves various purposes in woodworking and construction, offering precision and effectiveness in tasks requiring gentle yet impactful percussion.
A bundle of seeds for mammoth gold pumpkin plant. Opening this seed bundle will allow the crop to be planted by your faction.
One of the biggest varieties of pumpkin, the mammoth gold can grow to between 25 and 50 Kg of weight. Technically a giant berry, pumpkins are renowned for being trivial to both sow and harvest.
A mammoth's tusk. Very durable and valuable. Deadly but somewhat unwieldy as a weapon.
Wool from a woolly mammoth. Provides great protection from cold and looks mighty stylish.

An extremely large, genetically-engineered worm. Despite its incredibly intimidating size and arsenal, these huge creatures are designed to be peaceful. It was once part of the worker caste of the black hive, an artificial ecosystem of insectoids designed to fight mechanoid invasions. It carried and moved things that its little cousins cannot.

While generally peaceful, if provoked, it becomes a terrifying force that can rival those of mechanoid centipedes. Originally, the mammoth worm was specifically bred to destroy mechanoid structures, and as such it can be extremely effective against buildings. These insects can cause additional damage to mechanoids.
A fertilized mammoth worm egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby mammoth worm. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a worm egg, so it's disgusting either way...
An unfertilized mammoth worm egg. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a worm egg, so it's disgusting either way...

A floating, ticking time bomb that produces extremely reactive chemicals instead of chemfuel. Arguably more of a complex chemical distillery than an animal, it's a scientific miracle that it doesn’t explode every time it coughs. Surprisingly effective in combat in ways the enemy would really have preferred not knowing.

A humanoid hybrid with recessive boomalope genes. Thanks to its sac filled with buoyant chemicals, this hybrid never touches the ground and simply floats from location to location. Ignores terrain penalty costs and traps, while also being able to set down explosive traps of its own.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Humanoid hybrids will periodically engage other colonists in conversation, talking about a variety of topics. This increases the social recreation needs of those they interact with by 10% (subject to diminishing returns like all joy types). If using Ideology, humanoid hybrids are subject to precepts. Set trap ability: once every 3 days the manalope can set up an explosive IED. Hovers over terrain, ignoring terrain costs, and doesn't trigger ANY traps.

What it lacks in ferocity, it makes up for in tenacity and formidable cuteness. What person, sane or insane, could reject the diplomatic arguments presented by a waist-high teddy bear with a face just begging to be pinched. Not that you actually would, as those sharp teeth remind one that it very likely prefers to debate with its food before eating it.

A humanoid hybrid with recessive ursine genes. Absolutely terrible in combat potential despite its genetic material, but it is surprisingly adept at convincing prisoners to join the colony.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Humanoid hybrids will periodically engage other colonists in conversation, talking about a variety of topics. This increases the social recreation needs of those they interact with by 10% (subject to diminishing returns like all joy types). If using Ideology, humanoid hybrids are subject to precepts. Menbear are adept conversationalists and will help in recruiting prisoners.

A creature originally designed for other recreational purposes before that particular laboratory of degenerates got glassed from orbit, they make for an affectionate conversation partner. You know, probably, most likely, until their particular speech pattern grinds on your nerves like a cheese grater.

A humanoid hybrid with recessive feline genes. A surprisingly large yet timid predator that can output a disturbing amount of damage. Typically fun to talk to, but 10% of the time it tries to be a little too cute.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Like all cat hybrids, they have an improved melee dodge ability and a short nuzzle period. Humanoid hybrids will periodically engage other colonists in conversation, talking about a variety of topics. This increases the social recreation needs of those they interact with (subject to diminishing returns like all joy types). In the case of the mancat, these interactions will 90% of the time increase the targets' social joy by 15%, but the rest of the time they'll just make the target very annoyed... If using Ideology, humanoid hybrids are subject to precepts.
These are small curtains measuring 2x1. They are perfect for covering windows.

“You know how, like, chicken tastes, like, so good? So what if, like, we made a chicken that, y’know, when you killed it you could, I dunno, stuff it right in your mouth as fried chicken? Dude, this shit is the shit, where did you get this, man?” - Recording playback used in a hearing against a disgraced genetic scientist for misappropriating government funding.

A humanoid hybrid with recessive avian genes. A very valuable hybrid that convinces people that its greatest desire in life is to be eaten. When butchered, it leaves large amounts of completely healthy and nutritious meat that can be eaten as-is.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Humanoid hybrids will periodically engage other colonists in conversation, talking about a variety of topics. Doesn't lay eggs, but can be butchered for large amounts of a very nutritive meat that doesn't have poisoning chance and takes 6 days to rot.

Mandrills are one of the largest of all monkeys. They are shy and reclusive primates that live only in rain forests. Mandrills are extremely colorful, perhaps more so than any other mammal. They are easily identifiable by the blue and red skin on their faces and their brightly hued rumps.

Considered a straight upgrade from their progenitor, featured several times in Cannibal Monthly. Produces appreciable amounts of wool and milk, it is a living, breathing reference to the phrase “what does not kill me makes me stronger”. At least, when it comes to hauling large loads, which is all some people care about.

A humanoid hybrid with recessive muffalo genes. Capable of surviving very high temperatures in opposition to the traditional use of muffalos, this hybrid performs below average for a pack animal. However, due to adaptive muscle and skeletal structure, the more it participates as part of a caravan, the heavier the load it can withstand.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Humanoid hybrids will periodically engage other colonists in conversation, talking about a variety of topics. This increases the social recreation needs of those they interact with by 10% (subject to diminishing returns like all joy types). If using Ideology, humanoid hybrids are subject to precepts. The manffalo starts as a poor caravaning animal, but learns as time progresses. Every hour spent in a caravan will increase its cargo capacity by 1%, up to a maximum of a 100% increase from base.

An oval fruit, vividly coloured with shades of red and yellow. The single large seed is flattened, and the flesh that surrounds it is yellow to orange in colour, juicy, and of distinctive sweet-spicy flavour.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Mangoes cannot be frozen or they get destroyed. The game won't be smart enough to detect this, so disable them from freezers.

A compact logistics emitter that focuses local gravitic fields into four manipulator beams. With one colonist at the console, it can gather loose goods, corpses, and other haulables from afar and feed them straight into storage.

Blast turret is designed for close range area damage. It launches a burst of 3 frag grenades at a time. Beware of friendly fire. The manned version gives a slight increase to range and accuracy at the expense of an exposed operator.

A highly calibrated gun turret with high armor penetration. Advanced optics allows it to deliver precise single shots at long distances. The manned version gives a noticable increase to range and accuracy at the expense of an exposed operator.

A more powerful variant of an automated turret. Longer dual barrels provide increased accuracy, and greater burst. A staple weapons platform in any large colony. The manned version gives a noticable increase to range and accuracy at the expense of an exposed operator.

A powerful chain shotgun turret that fires volleys in quick succession. Shredder turret is designed for close range. It doesn't explode when destroyed, thus making it a perfect choice for indoor defense. The only downside is its rather large size. The manned version gives a noticable increase to range at the expense of an exposed operator.

A basic mannequin used to measure and shape garments for more refined results. Increases work speed when placed near a tailoring bench. Mannequin stand allows for more precise measurements, reducing the cost of crafting apparel by 10%. One workbench can only use one mannequin.

They say you can learn a lot by taking something apart and putting it back together again. Not this creature, it doesn’t give a damn, it just wants to take things apart because the hardest part is someone else’s problem. Some people actually prefer these chitinous creatures over actual humans as they’re not going to use up good material in a botched attempt.

An insectoid hybrid with recessive humanoid genes. Easy to train, quite resilient but not a great combatant. This particular hybrid fills the niche of fulfilling deconstruction orders around the colony, freeing up otherwise valuable manpower.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Humanoid hybrids will periodically engage other colonists in conversation, talking about a variety of topics. This increases the social recreation needs of those they interact with by 10% (subject to diminishing returns like all joy types). If using Ideology, humanoid hybrids are subject to precepts. All insectoid hybrids have good armor and no toxic sensitivity, but they are always sterile and can't reproduce, even if a fertility booster is used to create them. Menscarab will take building deconstruction orders around the colony.

A bloody weird little thing that hates the cold with a passion, and will take any opportunity to clear away snow from its home. Given that they are active at nighttime, they make a great conversational companion for those otherwise asocial Night Owls you keep gathering.

A humanoid hybrid with recessive rodent genes. Quite quick for their size and unusually a nocturnal animal, they make for a fast, social and quick-breeding hybrid. Will shovel snow if there are Clear Snow zones set up.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Humanoid hybrids will periodically engage other colonists in conversation, talking about a variety of topics. This increases the social recreation needs of those they interact with by 10% (subject to diminishing returns like all joy types). If using Ideology, humanoid hybrids are subject to precepts. The mansquirrel is a nocturnal animal that sleeps during the day. Will obey orders to clear snow around the colony.

Mixing the genes of one of the biggest carnivorous birds ever existing and those of a praying mantis is either a genious idea, or anathema. The Mantistanis stalks its prey by standing incredibly still and launching itself to attack with lightning speed.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All insectoid hybrids have good armor and no toxic sensitivity, but they are always sterile and can't reproduce, even if a fertility booster is used to create them. Slight regenerative properties.
Fertilized mantistanis egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked. If all goes well, it should hatch into a mantistanis.
Unfertilized mantistanis egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.
A light cloak covering shoulders and neck, providing some protection from the elements.

A mobile plant that was created as an attempt to weaponize venus flytraps by implanting concentrated formic acid spit launchers on its jaws. This strong acid is sometimes powerful enough to corrode the plasteel on mechanoid carapaces.

Possibly either the ancestor to the warg or an attempt at creating a successor, the team in charge of making this particular hybrid clearly had read one to many mythological novels. Arguably there’s no transformation at the full moon, so you just get the permanent single form, but there’s no pleasing some people.

A humanoid hybrid with recessive canine genes. A fast and dangerous hunter with almost misplaced self-confidence. Also very intelligent and possessing faint regenerative capabilities. Extremely hardy but also extremely restrictive in their diet.

A katana made to be as sharp and as beautiful as any blade in existence. Legend says that a Masamune is a divine sword made to protect all life from evil.
A simple dish made with boiled potatos then mashed into a soft mixture while supplmented with milk for a creamy base.

An advanced implant which allows a mechanitor to tap into the aggregate overmind and steal bandwidth from mech-hives. This significantly increases the number of mechanoids a single mechanitor can support.

These raw hides and pelts were removed from a creature, and with the right skills and tools, could be processed into tanned leather.

Usually a miserable, weak creature that oozes pus and struggles to keep breathing for longer than a few days. Sometimes, however, a genetic horror manages to survive, and even thrive. Perhaps it was released into the wild, where it managed to stabilize and grow. Or it subdued and devoured its creators. In any case, it has now turned into a pulsating, fleshy behemoth with a ravenous appetite.

Mature genetic horrors swallow their prey whole, storing up to 5 creatures in its huge stomach for later consumption. Prey can survive for up to one day, but they'll later be consumed and expelled as skeletonized remains.
A thick emulsion of egg, oil, and other herbs. Applying the mayo to a gourmet meal will grant it a mood-boosting effect while also making the consumer less hungry for twelve hours.

A creamy, smooth emulsion made from oil, egg yolks, and an acid like vinegar.

The small military backpack is broken.

Fermented beverage of deep golden colouring, a real lifeblood of social life in these parts. Few mugs in the tavern are all what's needed to forget about hardships of field work, dangers awaiting on the road or ill-considered marriage vows. Let the warm haze of drunkenness embrace you, no need to worry about anything. Not today.

A large flightless bird with colorful feathers that are mostly found in the plains eating fruits and berries. Because of their wildly colorful plumage, meadow aves naturally attract the eyes and hands of those who wander by. Many forget that underneath the majestic feathery coat is a wild animal with a razor sharp beak and claws to match.

Meadow aves are amazing mounts, much faster than horses. If properly trained, they can be ridden into battle at incredible speeds.

An unfertilized ave egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
Raw butchered flesh. Can be cooked into meals, or eaten raw.

The meadow lizard is a beast bred for speed. Even though they are naturally slower than meadow aves, they can be trained to be incredibly fast mounts.

Useful abilities: if properly trained they can be ridden into battle at incredible speeds (this interaction needs the Giddy-Up, combat mounts mod, and it will make the Meadow Lizards move 100% faster when used as mounts). They are also venomous.
Fertilized meadow lizard egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby meadow lizard. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

Despite being originally designed as an alternative to traditional raising of livestock, the technology is compatible with the physiology of nearly all animal species, including humans. The amount of meat produced depends on the amount of food consumed by its host.

This highly sought-after booster will result in an almost perfect hybrid: fertile, draftable and genetically stable.

This booster can't be crafted, only scavenged.

This strange stellated octahedron seems to house an assembly of complex computer chips. It appears to be self-powered, and a faint beeping noise emanates from its core. It is constantly emitting encoded radio waves, and perhaps these could be suitably amplified if the technology behind it could be properly reverse engineered.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Mechanoid chips can only be found in abandoned labs, and can be used to build biomechanical lab beacons, that will allow you to find a biomechanical lab complex, as well as mechahybrid antennas.

Should two exist per colonist enough signal noise will soft reset ancient mechanoid programming, causing an immediate retreat. This will only work on raiding mechanoids, clusters and
mechanoids won't be affected.

This diminutive egg seems to be metallic in nature at first, yet it is soft enough to crush it between two fingers. Once thus crushed it can be swallowed normally, and the active mechanites inside have a reinvigorating effect on the consumer. This effect can be slightly addictive, though.
An object with ideoligious significance.
This metallic, quicksilver-like substance is not edible. It can be processed in a refinery to obtain neutroamine, chemfuel and a bit of silver.

A mechanoid power generation unit. The vanometric power core will run forever, extracting energy from quantum foam fluctuations.

Can be obtained through careful deconstruction of an unstable power cell.

A specialized stasis container designed for the safe storage of mechanoids. Placing a mechanoid inside completely severs its active neural link with the mechanitor and puts its systems into deep suspended animation. In this state, the machine consumes no power and does not occupy the mechanitor's bandwidth, freeing up valuable network resources. The container allows you to keep an assault or worker squad in reserve, ready for deployment at a moment's notice without risking network overload.
This wool seems to be strengthened by plasteel micro-fibers, and covered with advanced circuitry.

The subpersona can perform certain tasks and calculations necessary to command and maintain large mechanoid groups on its own, allowing the mechinator to instead focus on ones not doable by a machine.

A brain implant of such complexity requires time to synchronize with and adapt to its host in order to avoid excessive strain on the central nervous system, its effectiveness will slowly increase during this process. It's capable of syncing with other enhancements made to assist in similar tasks, greatly increasing efficiency.

A heavy plasteel-weave helmet integrated with mechanoid-coordination systems. Enhances the wearer’s general control over of allied mechanoids, increasing mechanitor bandwidth and command groups while providing moderate protection.

A backpack containing an advanced bandwidth-expansion computer and antenna. Increases a mechanitor's maximum total bandwidth and control groups. When fueled with steel, it can construct small mechanoids that operate independently without consuming bandwidth. Each mechanitor can deploy up to two satellite mechanoids simultaneously.

A power-assisted armor suit packed with mechanitor-assistance gear. The mechmancer suit dramatically amplifies a mechanitor's bandwidth, providing a personal energy shield and damage resistance comparable to dedicated power armor.

A high-tech device that can be installed into a nose or any compatible artificial nose replacement. A miniaturised, implanted mechanoid gestator that allows the mechanitor to produce reinforcements in the field, without infrastructure or complex components.

This implant can be self-installed without surgery.

This implant can be installed up to 6 times to increase its capacity.

A bag with everything needed to provide medical treatment.

A standard battletank with decent armor in all sides, with the thinnest plating at the rear. Has a medium fuel efficiency, performs better in difficult terrain, and is quite visible.

A high-tech device that can be installed into any compatible artificial spine replacement. This particular module is capable of projecting a bubble-like barrier for the purpose of containing the swarm of healing nanites and aerosolized glitterworld drugs that it releases when active. Anyone within its range will slowly have their non-permanent wounds and injuries healed. Needs to be loaded with glitterworld medicine in order to function.

The unusual royal farm bird, the megachicken is raised by spoiled royalty as a pet project. This bird simply never stops growing, and if taken care of, it can reach gargantuan sizes. Royalty is known to compare their megacocks, and usually the one with the biggest specimen wins. Those that lose often argue that it’s not about the size, it’s about what you do with it.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Megachicken have five growth stages, at 0, 3, 8, 12 and 18 years of age. Their abilities get increasingly powerful as they age.
A fertilized megachicken egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a megachicken. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
An unfertilized megachicken egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.
An unfertilized megafauna egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.

A payload of megafauna genetic material. Can be used at the genomorpher to create a growth cell of a hybrid animal. This tier 2 genome can only be used as primary genome.

<color=#E5E54C>Extraction:</color> Can be extracted via a megafauna genome excavator from:

A simplified genome extraction device designed to be usable by even the most simple-minded goon, as such it resembles a caulking gun that works in reverse. The best genetic material can be found in the brain and the automated, single-use design instantly compresses this material into a usable genome.

The desired subject needs to be docile and trusting of the user who intends on scooping out their brain in a process that is not-quite instantaneous. It is recommended to anesthetize the creature as any sudden movement on their part will interrupt the whole process. Alternatively, it will also work on a dead body...

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> This excavator can be used to acquire the following genomes:

Long extinct giant reptiles, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The biggest terrestial lizard of all time, as well as the biggest venomous vertebrate that's ever existed.
Because of its relatively short legs, most of megalania's prey can easily outrun it, which is why it most often has to rely on the element of surprise in its hunts.
Fertilized megalania egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby megalania. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
A large stone used to construct a prehistoric structure or monument, either alone or together with other stones, often hewn in definite shapes for special purposes.

Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Despite being colloquially known as the 'Giant Elk', it's, in fact, not an elk but an enormous deer.
Megaloceros is an easily angered herbivore that can cause severe wounds with its extraordinarily large antlers, which are otherwise used exclusively for attracting females.
A dead megaloceros' pair of antlers. Great as a decoration, way too unwieldy to be used as a weapon.

Long extinct giant reptiles, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest tortoise of all time.
There aren't many predators that pose a threat to megalochelys, thanks to its thick and hard as rock shell. The ones that attempt to attack it anyway, will have to be prepared to deal with its surprisingly powerful bite.
Fertilized megalochelys egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby megalochelys. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

A large genetically engineered pill bug. These creatures once served as the frontline skirmishers of a genetically modified insectoid hive made as a weapon against mechanoid invasions. Their job consisted of reducing lone mechanoid infantry to shreds. Even centipedes were no match against the swarm of spikes.

Nowadays, they can be found roaming in packs much smaller than their former numbers and with killer instincts that yearn to be reawakened once more. These insects can cause additional damage to mechanoids.
A fertilized megalouse egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby megalouse. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a louse egg, so it's disgusting either way...
An unfertilized megalouse egg. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a louse egg, so it's disgusting either way...

Not actually a midge, the megamidge is a genetically-engineered giant insectoid adapted for extreme cold. In freezing temperatures, deadly cryogenic blades extend from its limbs, allowing it to deliver devastating slashes that inflict deep wounds and crippling crypto slowdown. However, when exposed to warmth, its blades retract, and it becomes sluggish and far less dangerous. Agile and lethal in the cold, but vulnerable in heat.

Long extinct giant arthropods, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The biggest flying insect to ever exist, meganeura, just like modern dragonflies, is a highly specialised predator.
Swift and agile, it used to have no aerial competition, which was one of the reasons why it had evolved to be so gigantic.
Fertilized meganeura egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a meganeura larva. It can be eaten raw, but it tastes horrible.

A giant, heavy insectoid that glides on dozens of tiny legs. Its thick chitin armor and sharp mandibles the size of an elephant’s tusk make it an excellent siege machine. Due to being extremely slow, they are somewhat vulnerable to hit-and-run tactics.

A colossal, herd-dwelling herbivore adapted to the harshest cold environments. The megareindeer boasts enormous, intricately branched antlers used for both display and defense. Originally engineered for arctic survival, it serves as a robust pack animal, capable of carrying heavy loads across frozen landscapes. Its thick, insulated fur is prized for crafting warm clothing. Generally docile, the megareindeer will fiercely maul enemies with its massive antlers if threatened.

A giant, genetically-engineered scorpion. Once created as a perfect assassination tool, it is not often seen returning to it's natural habitat - desert. A very potent poison in it's stinger helps it in tacking even much bigger prey. A eusocial creature, it cannot reproduce individually.

The Megatardi is a massive and curious creature, mutated from its tiny tardigrade origins to become a behemoth of the wasteland. Though slow and blind, it requires very little sustenance to survive and can consume even the most toxic wastepacks. With its six legs, the Megatardi is an impressive sight, and its gentle nature makes it a popular pack animal among those brave enough to venture into the polluted world. Though it is easily tamed, the Megatardi is not without its dangers. Upon its death, it releases a cloud of toxic gas, making it a potential hazard for anyone nearby. Despite this, the Megatardi remains a valuable asset for those willing to take on the challenges of the polluted wasteland.

A large, genetically-engineered thrips. A worker caste of an artificial ecosystem of insectoids designed to fight against humans in large scale wars, it now often makes up for the majority of the kemian geneline hives. Megathrisp uses sharp mandibles to rip the armor into shreds, while overcharged acid glands coat the exposed flesh in corrosive substance, causing severe burns. A eusocial creature, it cannot reproduce individually.

Not actually a wasp, the megawasp is a genetically-engineered giant flying insectoid the size of a cow. Designed as the hunter and the hive defender, megawasp soars through the air to engage enemies in close quarters, where it uses long and sharp ripper-blades and mandibles to cut anyone they face into pieces. The sharpness of the claws means that they are capable of eliminating even the most heavily armored enemies. It is, however, quite slow in open terrain.

A giant, genetically-engineered predator with massive paws to rip apart prey. Thick fur allows it to survive the coldest of climates, whilst it strength allows it to hunt even the largest of mammals for food.
Raw butchered flesh. Can be cooked into meals, or eaten raw.
a beautiful bed for babies.

An implant that enhances the combative capabilities of its host. The implant is crafted from the archometallic seed of a metalhorror, using an archotech shard to control and manipulate the growth of the creature. The symbiont’s metallic filaments weave through the host’s body, forming a second musculature system and the metalblood flowing through the host’s veins hardens in response to physical trauma. Due to the symbiont’s presence, any attempt by other metalhorrors to colonise the host will be rapidly destroyed. Upon death, the mechanisms that slave the metalhorror to the host will fail, allowing it to immediately tear free of the corpse.

A repulsive creature genetically modified to fill a very specific niche - eating metals. The tentacles in its mouth secrete an organic substance that is capable of rusting and dissolving most common metals, turning them into small flakes that serve as sustenance. They prefer small chunks of metal, since they can be more easily digested, but they will resort to digging into rocks in search of new metal if there is none available. Presumably, they were created to get rid of scrap metal, but they are mostly found in the wild now.
A large, soft, comfy seat. Great for relaxation. Can be used at tables, work stations, and elsewhere.
A cozy mattress and sheets on a frame for resting.
A backless bench that can seat many people. It is not very comfortable.
A backless bench that can seat many people. It is not very comfortable.
A soft-topped bounded table for playing a variety of billiards-type games. It trains shooting ability.
A small bin to help keep the surrounding area somewhat clean. Slowly removes trash and filth in a 10-cell radius.
A comfortable and attractive chair. Can be used at tables, work stations, and elsewhere.

The ancient game of kings. Fun for a few hours here and there, even playing alone. It trains intellectual skills.

This building requires adjacent chairs or stools to use.

A bulky, outdated computer standing on a small desk. The screen flickers, the keys stick, and it hums with age, but it still runs simple programs. There's always some archaic software waiting to be used.
A large double-wide seat which is cushioned for maximum comfort. Perfect for a luxurious rec room or a homey reading nook.
A simple double-wide bed that fits two people.
A small bedside table which makes nearby beds a little bit more comfortable. Must be placed directly adjacent to the head of the bed. Placing more than one end table near the same bed has no effect.
A high-tech flat-screen television with crystal-clear image and rich color. Picks up transmissions from ancient satellites and ubiquitous data cards.
A high-intensity light that's good for large outdoor spaces.
A locker for storing personal belongings. It improves the comfort of the bedroom.
プライバシーを守る目隠しです。
A partition that provides privacy. It makes the bedroom more comfortable.
Plant decorative flowers here to improve the mood of people nearby.

A table designed for playing gambling card games like poker. A great way to test your strategic skills and a bit of luck.

This building requires adjacent chairs or stools to use.

An industrial-era radio for playing music and spoken broadcasts. Even on the rimworlds, there is often an old transmitter running something at least marginally interesting. Provides passive music recreation to those that can hear it.
A carpet used to decorate floors.
A carpet used to decorate floors.
A carpet used to decorate floors.
A carpet used to decorate floors.
A carpet used to decorate floors.
A carpet used to decorate floors.
Produces power by consuming chemfuel. Must be periodically refueled by hand.
An electrical standing lamp that lights an area. People need light to move and work at full speed.
A simple platform on which to sit. Not very comfortable, but much better than nothing. Can be used at tables, work stations, and elsewhere.
A table with a mirror and styling tools. People can use this to change their look.
People eat off tables when chairs are placed facing them.
People eat off tables when chairs are placed facing them.
